results.name: Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Begin by lying across a bench, with only your upper back and shoulders supported. Your feet should be flat on the floor, and your hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats, following the same arc as you lowered it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
Ensure your upper back and shoulders are firmly supported on the bench.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far behind your head to prevent shoulder strain.
results.description: Dumbbell Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Renegade Row
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your feet hip-width apart and each hand holding a dumbbell, arms fully extended, and body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lift your right hand off the floor, rowing the dumbbell towards your right hip by bending your elbow and keeping your arm close to your body.
Lower the dumbbell back to the floor with control, returning to the plank position.
Repeat the row with your left hand. Alternate arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a straight body line, avoiding any sagging or lifting of the hips.
Keep your core engaged to prevent your body from rotating during the row.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Renegade Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Chest.

results.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing your thighs). Keep your arms straight and the dumbbells close to your body.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your hips back and lowering the dumbbells towards the floor. Keep a slight bend in your knees and maintain a neutral spine.
Lower the dumbbells until the dumbbells reach just under your knees or until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Push through your heels to extend your hips and return to the starting position, bringing the dumbbells back to your thighs. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on hinging at the hips rather than bending at the waist.
Keep the dumbbells close to your body throughout the movement for better control.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees to reduce stress on your lower back.
results.description: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Quadriceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Bent Over Row (Pronated Grip)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips. Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Pull the dumbbells towards your hips, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a moment, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
results.description: Dumbbell Bent Over Row (Pronated Grip) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbells Bent Over Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips. Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Pull the dumbbells towards your hips, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a moment, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
results.description: Dumbbells Bent Over Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbells Plank to Alternating Row
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your hands gripping a dumbbell each on the floor, directly under your shoulders, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Your feet should be slightly wider than hip-width apart for stability.
Keeping your core tight, lift the right dumbbell off the floor, rowing it towards your right hip while balancing on your left hand and feet.
Lower the dumbbell back to the floor with control, returning to the high plank position.
Repeat the rowing motion with your left hand, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your body as you row.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the exercise.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form without compromising balance.
results.description: Dumbbells Plank to Alternating Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbells Single Arm Row
instructions: Place your left knee and left hand on a bench, lean your torso down to almost parallel to the floor. Your right foot should be planted firmly on the floor, knee bent and slightly behind for balance. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, arm extended towards the floor.
Pull the dumbbell towards your hip by bending your elbow, keeping it close to your body. Focus on squeezing your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arm with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to perform the exercise with your left arm.
tips: Avoid rotating your torso as you row; keep your core engaged to maintain stability.
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbell.
Ensure your supporting knee and hand are positioned securely on the bench for stability.
results.description: Dumbbells Single Arm Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Elbow Lift Reverse Push Up
instructions: Sit on the floor between two chairs, with your torso facing the ceiling and your elbows resting on the chairs, arms bent at 90 degrees.
Extend your legs out in front of you, keeping them together and straight, and lift your hips into a reverse plank position, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your heels.
Press through your elbows to lift your torso and hips slightly higher, engaging your triceps and core muscles.
Lower your body back down by bending your elbows, keeping your torso and legs straight throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the chairs are stable and securely placed to prevent slipping or tipping during the exercise.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement and avoid injury.
Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and support your lower back.
results.description: Elbow Lift Reverse Push Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest, Triceps.

results.name: Exercise Ball Back Extension With Hands Behind Head
instructions: Position yourself face down on an exercise ball with your hips resting on the ball and your feet anchored against a wall or stable surface for balance.
Place your hands behind your head, elbows pointing out to the sides.
Engage your core and lower your upper body towards the floor, rounding your back slightly.
Lift your upper body back up until your body forms a straight line from your head to your hips. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on lifting with your back muscles rather than pulling with your hands to avoid neck strain.
Breathe steadily, inhaling as you lower your body and exhaling as you lift it.
Ensure your feet are firmly anchored to prevent slipping and maintain balance.
Avoid overextending your back at the top of the movement to prevent strain.
results.description: Exercise Ball Back Extension With Hands Behind Head is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Good Mornings Barbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip.
Begin to hinge at your hips, pushing your hips back while lowering your torso towards the floor.
Continue to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor.
Return to the starting position by driving your hips forward and raising your torso back up. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a straight back and avoid rounding your spine.
Focus on hinging at the hips rather than bending at the waist.
Keep a slight bend in your knees to reduce stress on your lower back.
results.description: Good Mornings Barbell is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.
